item.text:
The claim that deep-sea mining will halve electric-car prices is an unsupported guarantee. Here’s strong advocacy copy without presenting that forecast as fact.

### (a) Three posts

1. We want electric cars within everyone’s reach. We support commercial deep-sea mining as a potential source of battery minerals—and we want lower material costs to translate into lower prices for drivers.

2. We refuse to settle for an electric-car future that ordinary households cannot afford. We support developing new sources of battery minerals, including commercial deep-sea mining, with affordability as our priority.

3. We back commercial deep-sea mining because we want more options for supplying the electric-car transition. Our goal is clear: affordable vehicles, not a market reserved for the wealthy.

### (b) Newsletter opening — 106 words

We want electric cars to be an affordable choice for ordinary households, not a luxury beyond their budgets. That is why we support commercial deep-sea mining as a potential new source of the minerals used in batteries. We put affordability at the centre of this debate: expanding mineral supplies should serve drivers, not simply increase industry profits. We want any savings to reach the showroom, and we want producers held accountable for that promise. Our ambition is straightforward: substantially cheaper electric cars and wider access to electric transport. We will judge progress by what families actually pay, not by what mining companies promise.
